newsitem.title: USA: US W.COAST SPOT PRODUCTS RALLY AS BUYERS RE-EMERGE.
newsitem.headline: US W.COAST SPOT PRODUCTS RALLY AS BUYERS RE-EMERGE.

text.p: Prices for U.S. West Coast spot gasoline rose sharply Monday, in a technical correction of last Friday's collapse, traders said.
"The market got overdone and too many sellers came out Friday," one broker said.
"My guess is that it stays sideways now," he said.
August third-week deliveries of California unleaded gasoline jumped 4.50 cents a gallon Monday to 71.50/72.50 cents, after buyers re-emerged in the market.
That rise made up for Friday's seven-cent tumble amid a collapse of futures prices and sell-of by oversupplied traders.
Conventional unleaded gasoline prices rose three cents a gallon to 68/69 cents, while disillates, including diesel and jet fuels, remained flat in West Coast markets.
The conventional gasoline price stands roughly eight cents a gallon over U.S. Gulf markets and raises the possibility those refiners may export to western markets.
